meta.description: Once a day, reads Instagram Insights for every client with analytics enabled — account metrics, follower count and per-post metrics for the last 30 days — stores them as history in the portal, then refreshes the AI recommendations.

parameters.content:
## Daily Instagram Insights

**What it does**
Every morning, for each client: read account metrics for *yesterday*, read metrics for posts from the last 30 days, store both as history, then regenerate the AI recommendations.

**Why yesterday, not today**
Instagram's day-scoped metrics for the current day are still accumulating. Storing them would record a partial day as a real one and put a fake trough at the end of every chart.

**Why the portal picks the posts**
It already knows which media it published and when, so the workflow only spends Graph API calls on posts still inside the freshness window instead of walking the whole feed.

**Rate limits**
Meta allows 200 calls/user/hour. This spends roughly 4 + 2×(posts) per client. The batching below keeps a 20-client agency well inside that.

### Account-level metrics

Three calls because Meta splits them:
- plain `period=day` metrics
- `metric_type=total_value` metrics (most of the interaction ones)
- `follower_count`, which is a daily delta

plus one field read for the running follower total.

All are `neverError` — an account that can't serve one metric must not cost us the other three.

### Per-post metrics

n8n runs an HTTP node once per input item, so expanding the media list into items is all the looping this needs — no inner Loop node.

Post metrics are Instagram's **lifetime** totals, not daily figures. The portal stores one row per post per day so a chart can show either the running total or the day-on-day change.

nodes.name: Daily at 06:30
nodes.notes: 06:30 local. Late enough that Meta has settled yesterday's numbers, early enough that the dashboard is current before the agency starts work.

nodes.name: Fetch clients & their posts
nodes.notes: GET /insights/targets — every client with analytics enabled and an IG account id, each with the media ids published in the last 30 days and (when it has one) its own access token.

nodes.name: Expand client list
nodes.notes: One item per client, each carrying the exact UTC day window and the token to use (its own, or the agency's).

nodes.name: One client at a time
nodes.notes: Serial rather than parallel: Meta rate-limits per user, and a burst of 20 clients × 30 posts would trip it. Output 0 = all clients done, output 1 = next client.

nodes.name: Account: reach & views
nodes.notes: The plain day-period metrics. `views` replaced `impressions` from v22 onwards; the portal's parser accepts either name, so this keeps working across API versions.

parameters.url: =https://graph.facebook.com/{{ $('One client at a time').item.json.api_version }}/{{ $('One client at a time').item.json.ig_user_id }}/insights

nodes.name: Account: engagement metrics
nodes.notes: Meta only serves these with metric_type=total_value, and rejects the whole call if ANY listed metric is unavailable for that account. neverError keeps a rejection as data so the run continues with whatever the other calls returned.

parameters.url: =https://graph.facebook.com/{{ $('One client at a time').item.json.api_version }}/{{ $('One client at a time').item.json.ig_user_id }}/insights

nodes.name: Account: follower change
nodes.notes: `follower_count` is the NET CHANGE for the day, not the total. Meta only serves it for accounts above 100 followers — smaller ones return an error, which neverError turns into a harmless zero.

parameters.url: =https://graph.facebook.com/{{ $('One client at a time').item.json.api_version }}/{{ $('One client at a time').item.json.ig_user_id }}

nodes.name: Account: follower total
nodes.notes: The running follower count — a field on the account, not an insight. Stored so the followers chart has an absolute line as well as a daily delta.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ client_id: $('One client at a time').item.json.client_id, date: $('One client at a time').item.json.snapshot_date, insights: { data: [].concat($('Account: reach & views').item.json.data || [], $('Account: engagement metrics').item.json.data || [], $('Account: follower change').item.json.data || []) }, followers: $json.followers_count || 0, posts_count: 0 }) }}

nodes.name: Store account snapshot
nodes.notes: The three insights responses are concatenated and passed through untouched — the portal's parser handles every shape Meta serves, so the fragile version-specific bit lives in tested code rather than in an n8n expression. Upserted by (client, date), so re-running the day is safe.

nodes.name: Expand media list
nodes.notes: Fans the client's media ids out into items. Emits a single no_media marker for a client with nothing published, so the outer loop still advances.

nodes.name: Any posts to read?
nodes.notes: False branch skips straight back to the loop for the next client.

nodes.name: Post: media object
nodes.notes: Runs once per media item. `like_count` and `comments_count` come from here rather than from insights — the media edge serves them even when the insights edge refuses a brand-new post, so they are the more reliable source.

nodes.name: Post: insights
nodes.notes: Lifetime metrics for one post. Meta serves different metric sets per media type and rejects the whole call on an unsupported one — neverError means such a post falls back to the like/comment counts from the media object instead of failing the client's whole batch.

nodes.name: Bundle post insights
nodes.notes: Re-pairs each media object with its insights response and collapses them into one payload — 1 write instead of N.

nodes.name: Store post insights
nodes.notes: One batched write per client. The endpoint reports partial success — a post whose insights Meta refused is skipped and named, the other twenty-nine still land.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ client_id: $('Bundle post insights').item.json.client_id, date: $('Bundle post insights').item.json.date, posts_count: $('Bundle post insights').item.json.posts_published_on_date }) }}

nodes.name: Record posts-per-day
nodes.notes: A second, tiny upsert on the same snapshot row, now that we know how many posts actually went out that day — the posting-frequency chart reads this. Separate call because the count is only knowable after the media objects have been fetched.

nodes.name: Next client
nodes.notes: Join point for both branches; returns to the loop.

nodes.name: Refresh AI recommendations
nodes.notes: Runs once, AFTER every client's numbers have landed — the advice is computed from those numbers, so running it first would recommend on yesterday's picture. 90 days, because 'best posting time' needs enough posts per weekday slot to be more than noise. Long timeout: this is one LLM call per client.

nodes.name: On workflow crash
nodes.notes: Analytics failing is not urgent — nothing is published and no client sees it — but a week of silent failure would leave every chart flat. This makes it visible in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Crash recorded
nodes.notes: Terminal. The failed execution is already in n8n's log; nothing to publish or undo. Add a Slack/email node here if you want to be told.
